review.review: The hero died to the great crab: decision 1966 accepted transition (log line 5659) reduced HP from 3 to 0, and terminal observation 5660 explicitly names the killer. Starvation was also observed. The fatal episode began earlier: after three doorway strikes, decisions 1774 and 1805 reported no admitted fresh surprise or escape-backed doorway, and recovery eventually waited beside the awake crab. Recharging alone could not defeat its guard. Separately, a supported initiating navigation defect wasted advancing turns before quest acceptance: the ghost was last observed at 731 in decision 1657; decision 1669 approached that already visibly empty cell, followed by the 690/691 orbit and navigation-loop at decision 1681. The proposed narrow correction declines this stale approach only after reaching interaction range and seeing the remembered cell empty. A reduced public-derived fixture reproduces the original selected cells; it is not a full runtime reconstruction. Six new regression tests fail with two expected assertions on original source and pass on the candidate; the full suite passes 1,546 tests with four skips. The correction does not establish safe ghost reacquisition or repair the fatal crab encounter. Pre-death potions remained unidentified; death-revealed identities are not usable preparation evidence. Mandatory progression pickup and pending reward return remain intact.
review.learnings: Do not orbit a remembered NPC coordinate after reaching interaction range and observing it empty. Preserve distant approach and mandatory reward return. For the crab stall, validate attempt and pursuit bookkeeping against recorded selections before testing a bounded surprise alternative; do not treat recharging or death-revealed potion identities as a solution.
